artists.name: Intigam Agayev
artists.bio:
Intigam Agayev was born in Sumgayit, Azerbaijan, in 1966. He studied at the Azerbaijan State Art School named after Azim Azimzade from 1983 to 1989.  
Throughout his career, Agayev has participated in numerous local and international exhibitions. He became a member of the Union of Artists of Azerbaijan in 2012 and held his solo exhibition My Memories at the Union’s exhibition hall in 2016.  
His artistic practice explores themes of memory, everyday life, nature, and historical experience. Since 2022, Agayev has been a member of the Caravan Art group

artists.name: Sabina Safarova
artists.bio: Sabina Safarova is an Azerbaijani artist born in Baku in 1982. She holds a Master’s degree in International and European Law from Western University and studied Fine Arts at the Azerbaijan State Academy of Art. Although trained in law, painting has remained a central part of her creative practice for over a decade. She has participated in exhibitions in Azerbaijan and internationally, including projects in Spain, Italy, Belgium and Luxembourg. Safarova is a member of the Union of Artists of Azerbaijan.
artists.statement: My artistic practice is centered on painting as a way of expressing emotions through color and form. After years of academic and professional development in law, I returned to formal art education and continued to develop painting as my primary means of expression. Through my work, I explore personal experience, emotions and the relationship between color, form and memory.

artists.name: Chinara Soltanova (Chinara Chi)
artists.bio:
Chinara Chi (Chinara Soltanova) is an Azerbaijani visual artist born in Shamakhi in 1996 and based in Azerbaijan. Her practice encompasses painting, experimental installations, video and mixed media.
She studied Philology at Baku State University and is currently pursuing a degree in Easel Painting at the Azerbaijan State University of Culture and Arts. Her background in literature plays an important role in her artistic approach and informs her interest in memory, cultural narratives and human experience.
Her work has been presented in group exhibitions and contemporary art platforms across Azerbaijan.
artists.statement: My practice focuses on the human figure and portraiture, exploring memory, psychological states, self-perception and belonging. I combine classical painting techniques with expressive distortion, layering and experimental surfaces. My work is also informed by literature, mythology, personal memory and the cultural history of my birthplace, Shamakhi.

artists.name: Emil Majnunov (Moosem135)
artists.bio:
Emil Majnunov (Moosem135) is a graffiti and contemporary artist born in Baku, Azerbaijan, in 1995. He began painting graffiti at the age of 13, marking the beginning of an artistic journey that has continued to evolve for over 17 years.
Over time, his practice has expanded into graphic design, illustration, paintings, murals, alongside an ongoing experimentation with different styles, techniques, and surfaces. What began as an interest in graffiti during his teenage years gradually became a way of life and an ongoing exploration of visual expression.
Working under the name Moosem135, Emil continues to explore the space between graffiti and contemporary art, drawing from years of practice, experimentation, and lived experience.
artists.statement: My work explores the space between graffiti and contemporary art through constant experimentation with styles, techniques, and surfaces. Drawing from years of graffiti, painting, illustration, and mural practice, I explore visual expression as a way to connect urban energy with contemporary art.

artists.name: Orkhan Garayev
artists.bio:
Orkhan Garayev (b. 1991, Ganja, Azerbaijan) is a contemporary Azerbaijani artist based in Baku. Working
across painting, graphic art, sculpture, installation, and book illustration, he explores the intersection of
cultural heritage and contemporary visual language. His practice is distinguished by symbolic imagery,
expressive color, and poetic narratives that reflect themes of memory, identity, and place. Garayev is a
member of the Union of Artists of Azerbaijan, the designer of official Azerbaijani postage stamps, and has
exhibited internationally. His works are held in public and private collections.
artists.statement: My works, including "Red", "Trapped Earth", and "Hope", are part of the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in Baku. I have presented my work at international exhibitions in Turkey, Germany, Russia, Georgia, Switzerland, France, the UAE, Luxembourg, and Belgium, connecting my artistic practice with audiences across different cultural contexts.

artists.name: Nigar Kerimova
artists.bio:
Nigar Karimova is a Baku-born Azerbaijani artist, founder of Benu Art Studio by Karimova and a member of the Union of Artists of Azerbaijan since 2017. She began drawing in childhood and held her first solo exhibition at the age of nine.

Her artistic practice combines Impressionism and Symbolism, focusing on inner psychological states, memory, instinct, identity, and the subconscious. She works primarily with oil and acrylic, as well as watercolor and mixed media.

Karimova has participated in numerous local and international exhibitions, including showcases in Barcelona and exhibitions at the Azerbaijan State Museum. Her works are held in private collections in Azerbaijan, Canada, the USA, Germany, Sweden, Russia, and Turkey.

She currently continues her artistic practice while directing Benu Art Studio by Karimova.
artists.statement:
My artistic practice explores memory, time, identity, and the invisible forces shaping human experience. Through painting and mixed media, I use symbolism and metaphor to transform familiar images into reflections of emotion, the subconscious, and personal memory.

Inspired by Baku and its cultural heritage, my work explores the connection between place, identity, and experience. I see art as a space for dialogue, inviting each viewer to discover their own meanings and emotions.

artists.name: Roza Muradova
artists.bio:
Roza Muradova is a contemporary painter based in Baku, Azerbaijan, working across oil, acrylic, ink, and watercolor. Her practice explores the relationship between movement, emotion, and the shifting boundary between abstraction and figuration.

Through expressive gestures, layered brushwork, and subtle use of texture, Muradova creates atmospheric compositions that evoke inner psychological states and fragmented memories. Her work often draws from nature as a source of rhythm and transformation, translating organic forms into intuitive visual language.

Her paintings have been exhibited internationally and are held in private collections worldwide.
artists.statement:
I approach painting as an intuitive process, allowing form and meaning to emerge through movement and spontaneity. Working in layers, I explore transformation, where forms appear, dissolve, and change, reflecting shifting emotions and perception.

Through minimal, deliberate gestures, I create open compositions that invite personal interpretation.

events.title: 7YA (SevenYouAre)
events.description: ROOM Baku and DaMir – House of Imagination present 7-YA (SevenYouAre), an art project held from September 8–14, 2025, in Ivanovka. For one week, seven artists — Vusala Agharaziyeva, Nigar Familsoy, Gunel Akhundlu, Orkhan Garayev, Sarkhan Gadzhiev, Mushfig Heydarov, and Rufana Mamedova — lived and worked together, exploring the multiplicity of the "Self." The name "7-YA" reflects the idea that within each person exists a multitude of states and roles. Seven participants, seven days, and seven facets of identity came together in paintings, sketches, and a collective installation shaped through dialogue, workshops, and shared creation. The exhibition is hosted at ROOM Baku — a wine house in the city center where wine culture meets art and gastronomy. Here, the artists' works and a video portrait of the project invite visitors to reflect on identity and the courage to be many at once.

events.title: A Person Between Two Worlds
events.description:
My artistic practice explores form, lettering, character, and the visual language of contemporary urban culture. Drawing from graffiti, street culture, graphic design, comics, and popular media, I combine familiar visual elements into new structures.

At the center of my work is a recurring male character, developed from my graffiti practice in 2014–2015. He embodies the tension between traditional values and contemporary urban life — a person whose body belongs to the present, while his mindset remains rooted in the past.

Through constantly changing techniques, colors, and styles, I use this character to explore identity, cultural heritage, social expectations, and the conflict between tradition and change.

Emil Moosem.

events.title: Vusala Agharaziyeva - Selected Works
events.description:
A collection of selected works by artist Vusala Agharaziyeva is now on view at ROOM, Baku Airport.
Discover the exhibition and experience art in the atmosphere of travel, where every journey can begin with a moment of inspiration.

about.concept: ROOM is a contemporary art space in the heart of Baku where art, wine, and culture come together through exhibitions, talks, and curated encounters.
about.vision: To support contemporary artists and build a thoughtful creative community around collecting, learning, and conversation.
about.identity: Minimal, neutral, atmospheric, and emotionally precise. ROOM places the artwork first and lets the digital experience behave like a gallery visit.
